M1.reason: Overlap is 0.80 or more in every view (0.845 front/back, 0.826 left/right, 0.903 top/below), but the outline is clearly off in places. In the left and right views the original's rounded, sloping head and arched back have become a boxy body with a flat top and a flat, cylinder-like front face. The haunch is squarer than the original's. In the front, back and top views the shoulder pads stick out as separate blocks beside the body, where the original's are flush.

M2.reason: Length, width and height are 49.6 x 33.9 x 44.7 against the original's 49.3 x 33.5 x 44.7. The largest difference is 0.9%, well inside 10%.

M3.reason: The main parts are there: the eye cluster at the front, three legs, the shoulder pads, the mouth underneath and the back spikes. The spikes are wrong, though. The original has about five broad, thick spikes; the reproduction has about seven or eight thin blades (left and right views). The shoulder pads are boxy blocks standing off the sides instead of rounded muscle on the body (front view, front-left and front-right views).

M4.reason: Mean ΔE is 12.9, under 15, and no view is above 15.4. The yellow-olive skin, the cyan and brown stripes, the pale belly with blue veins and the dark eye cluster are all in the original's colours.

M5.reason: The stripes, belly veins, eye cluster and mouth markings are there, but they are scrambled and soft. In the top view the original's regular cyan and brown bands have turned into broken, jagged chevrons. The side and angled views show the skin texture stretched and smeared on the boxy front and flanks, and the eye cluster is blurrier than the original's.

M6.reason: From the front and below it reads as a houndeye. From the side, which is how a player usually sees it, the box-shaped body, flat front, thin blade spikes and pads standing off the sides are noticeably wrong. A player would see it is not quite the original.

M7.reason: It faces the same way as the original, stands upright and its feet rest on the same ground line in every view.

M8.reason: The reproduction has 1214 triangles against the original's 308, about 3.9 times as many. The limit is twice the original's (616). SMAK's check reported no errors, but the triangle count alone fails this item.

C1.reason: In the run, the original hunches, tips forward and stretches out in a bounding gallop, its body curling and pitching from frame to frame. The reproduction's body stays rigid and level through all 22 frames while only the legs swing underneath. Nothing clearly comes apart or floats, but it does not move the way the original does. The thin spike blades also go streaky as it moves (Run2 6/22 to 22/22).
